name: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: India’s largest Buddhist monastery and the second-largest in the world, founded in 1680–81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso under the patronage of the 5th Dalai Lama. Perched at about 3,000 m overlooking the Tawang Chu valley, it belongs to the Gelug school and houses a large gilded Buddha statue and ancient manuscripts.
facts: Founded 1680–81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama
Requires Inner Line Permit for visitors

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at 4,170 m (13,700 ft) on the Tawang–West Kameng border, carrying NH-13 and serving as the main gateway to Tawang. Surrounded by snow-capped peaks and the often-frozen Sela Lake; the nearby Sela Tunnel provides all-weather connectivity.
facts: On border of Tawang and West Kameng districts
Sela Tunnel opened for year-round access
Named after local Monpa girl Sela
Mandatory stop on road to Tawang

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude glacial lake formed by a 1950s earthquake, featuring upright dead tree trunks rising from the water. Popularly known as Madhuri Lake after a film shoot; located on the road toward Bum La Pass amid pine forests and snow peaks.
facts: Formed by earthquake creating submerged forest
Army permit often required with Bum La visit

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: Spectacular 100-metre-high waterfall near Jang town on the Tawang–Sela route, cascading from glacial slopes. Named after local Monpa girl Nura; popular picnic spot with a small hydel unit nearby.

name: Bum La Pass
description: High-altitude border pass at about 4,600–4,800 m on the India–China Line of Actual Control, historically used by the 14th Dalai Lama in 1959. Requires special army and district permits; offers stark high-altitude views and is a Border Personnel Meeting point.
facts: Special permit from DC and Army required
Combine with Sangetsar Tso when permitted

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Nyingma monastery founded around 1489, recognized as the birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso in 1683. Smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, located near the town with traditional Tibetan architecture.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Memorial stupa and complex dedicated to soldiers of the 1962 Sino-Indian War, featuring light-and-sound shows, preserved weapons, and names of the fallen. Located near Tawang town with panoramic views.
facts: Light and sound show in evenings

name: Jaswant Garh Memorial
description: War memorial on the Tawang–Sela highway honouring Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of the 4th Garhwal Rifles, who held his post for 72 hours during the 1962 Battle of Nuranang and was awarded the Maha Vir Chakra posthumously. Maintained by the Indian Army.
facts: Honours Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat MVC
Army maintains the site as living memorial

name: Pankang Teng Tso (PT Tso)
description: Pristine high-altitude lake about 17 km from Tawang on the road to Bum La, surrounded by rhododendron forests and peaks. Freezes in winter; popular short stop for views and photography.

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main tourist base at about 3,000 m elevation, gateway to the monastery, lakes, and high passes. Home to Monpa culture, markets, and starting point for most circuits; requires Inner Line Permit.

name: Zemithang
description: Remote western valley and circle near the Bhutan border, known for Gorsam Chorten, Monpa villages, and scenic landscapes. Offbeat destination for cultural and nature experiences beyond the main Tawang circuit.
facts: About 85–90 km west of Tawang via Lumla

name: Chakzam Bridge
description: Ancient iron suspension bridge across the Tawang Chu River, attributed to the 15th-century Tibetan engineer Thangtong Gyalpo. Historic architectural landmark near the main routes.

name: Bomdila
description: District headquarters of West Kameng at about 2,530–2,700 m elevation, a key hill station and base on the Tezpur–Tawang highway. Known for apple orchards, Buddhist monasteries, craft centres, and panoramic Himalayan views; gateway for further circuits.
facts: Base for Dirang and Tawang circuits

name: Bomdila Monastery (GRL / Gontse Gaden Rabgyel Ling)
description: Prominent Gelug monastery complex in Bomdila with Upper and Lower Gompas, established as a centre of Buddhist learning and culture. Features traditional architecture, prayer halls, and a school; overlooks the town and surrounding ridges.
facts: Also known as Gontse Gaden Rabgyel Ling

name: Dirang
description: Scenic valley town and circle headquarters at about 1,500 m, known for apple and kiwi orchards, Dirang Dzong fort, hot springs, and Monpa culture. Popular overnight stop between Bomdila and Tawang with milder climate.
facts: Home to Dirang Dzong and hot springs

name: Dirang Hot Springs
description: Natural thermal springs near Dirang town, popular for bathing and relaxation amid the valley setting. One of the few easily accessible hot springs on the Tawang route.
facts: Accessible by short drive or walk

name: Sangti Valley
description: Beautiful high valley about 14 km from Dirang, surrounded by Eastern Himalayan ranges. Known for black-necked cranes in winter, terraced fields, Monpa villages, and scenic river landscapes; popular for birdwatching and photography.
facts: Best November to March for birds

name: Thembang Fortified Village (Thembang Dzong)
description: Historic fortified Monpa village on a ridge near Dirang, with stone walls, gates, and traditional houses. On UNESCO tentative World Heritage list since 2014; community-managed heritage site with homestays and cultural experiences.

name: Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Protected area of about 218 km² in the Himalayan foothills, renowned as one of India’s premier birding sites with over 450 bird species. Ranges from 500 to 3,250 m elevation; adjoins Sessa Orchid Sanctuary and supports red pandas, elephants, and rich biodiversity.
facts: Part of Kameng Protected Area Complex

name: Sessa Orchid Sanctuary
description: 100 km² orchid sanctuary established in 1989 along the Bhalukpong–Bomdila route, protecting over 200 orchid species including rare and endemic ones. Adjoins Eaglenest; features trekking routes, nursery, and diverse Himalayan habitats.

name: Tippi Orchid Research Centre
description: Major orchid research and conservation centre at Tippi on the banks of the Kameng River, about 6 km from Bhalukpong. Features glasshouses with thousands of orchids, museum, herbarium, and gardens; established 1972.
facts: Thousands of orchid species and hybrids

name: Nyukmadong War Memorial
description: War memorial commemorating the Battle of Nyukmadong on 18 November 1962, featuring a chorten-style stupa, plaques of fallen soldiers, and terraced landscaping. Located between Dirang and Sela Pass on the main highway.

name: Bhalukpong
description: Gateway town and entry point to Arunachal Pradesh from Assam at the foothills of the Kameng River, elevation about 213 m. Popular for picnic spots, permit processing, and start of the ascent to Bomdila and Tawang.
facts: Start of scenic drive to Bomdila

name: Mandala Top
description: Scenic hilltop near Dirang featuring a circular arrangement of 108 Buddhist stupas amid panoramic mountain views. Popular viewpoint and short excursion for photography and meditation.

name: Chillipam Monastery (Sangngag Choekhor Dargyeling)
description: Hilltop monastery near Rupa village offering spectacular 270-degree views of the valleys. Built on a promontory; significant centre of Tibetan Buddhism in West Kameng with traditional architecture.

name: Lhagyala Gompa
description: Historic monastery overlooking the Morshing valley, about 80 km from Bomdila. Traditional Tibetan Buddhist architecture with prayer flags and serene mountain setting.
facts: Official tourist place of the district

name: Shergaon
description: Offbeat village and circle area known for horticulture farms, apple orchards, megalithic sites like Kamcho Yam, and scenic rural landscapes. Base for nature and cultural exploration away from main highways.
